use: Use a button to trigger actions, events, or main workflows (such as submitting forms, confirming choices, or proceeding to the next step).
Buttons should be easy to locate, scan, and understand as actionable items.
Buttons can serve as entry points into deeper workflows, dialogs, or page transitions.
Buttons can be placed together in a row or grouped logically (such as primary and secondary actions in a footer).
Labels should clearly describe the action the button performs, optionally accompanied by leading or trailing icons for added context.
Buttons come in different variants (such as filled or outlined) and interactive states (default, hover, focus, disabled) to clearly communicate availability and interactivity.
dont: Don't use buttons for navigation links that take users to a different website or page content (use text links or navigational tabs instead).
Don't crowd too many high-priority buttons together; avoid having multiple primary buttons side-by-side in the same view.
Don't use buttons as static informational tags or badges where no action is performed.
Don't rely on icons alone inside a button without an accessible text label or tooltip, unless the icon's meaning is universally understood.
bestPractice: Adjust button placement and hierarchy so the primary call-to-action remains the main focus on the screen.
When designing forms or dialogs, consistently align primary actions (e.g., "Save" or "Submit") and secondary actions (e.g., "Cancel") following platform conventions.
Use distinct styles (such as fill vs. outline) to distinguish between primary and secondary actions.
Ensure buttons provide clear visual feedback across all states (hover, focus, active, and disabled).
Keep button text concise and action-oriented, typically starting with a strong verb.
Ensure touch targets on mobile devices are large enough to be easily tapped (minimum recommended size).
Support keyboard navigation with clear focus rings around buttons.
Maintain consistent spacing around buttons to prevent accidental clicks, especially on dense layouts or mobile screens.

unbound.note: Fixed height with no variable bound. Padding, gap, radius, colours and type on the same node are bound.

Card.description: Main container component for listing items, combining media previews, structured metadata, action controls, and layout arrangements.

use: Use a card to display content and actions on a single topic.
Cards should be easy to scan for relevant and actionable information.
Cards can serve as entry points into deeper levels of detail or navigation, such as a music album or details on an upcoming vacation.
Cards can be displayed together in a grid, vertical list, or carousel.
Use cards to contain related elements
Contents can include anything from images to headlines, supporting text, buttons, and lists
Can also contain other components in slot area.
Cards have flexible layouts and dimensions based on their contents. Configuration is done at subcomponent level: CardLayout.
dont: Don’t scroll within a card to reveal information
Cards shouldn’t contain content that can be swiped, such as an image carousel or pagination. Also, swipe gestures shouldn’t cause portions of cards to detach upon swiping.
Don’t let cards bump other elements out of the way. When a card is picked up, it appears in front of all elements, except app bars and navigation.
On a mobile device, cards can't internally scroll, as it could cause two scroll bars to be displayed.
bestPractice: Adjust the card layout so content remains the main focus on large screens
When designing for large screens, use multiple columns to display content
Certain devices or user contexts require different components to meet platform expectations
Expand a card to reveal information
A card should only have one swipe action assigned to it
When moving a card, increase its elevation
On a mobile device, cards can expand to reveal more content, scrolling within the screen. Content within cards doesn’t scroll.

sets.name: Card
sets.description: Main container component for listing items, combining media previews, structured metadata, action controls, and layout arrangements.

sets.name: CardContainer
sets.description: Base structural frame for card components that manages outer surface styling, elevation (shadows), borders, padding, and corner radius.

sets.name: CardLayout
sets.description: Structural layout container used to switch between horizontal (row) and vertical (column) arrangements for card components.

sets.name: CardImage
sets.description: Media subcomponent for cards that manages image display ratios, gradient overlays for contrast, and overlaid action buttons (e.g., favorite heart trigger).

sets.name: CardText
sets.description: Text metadata subcomponent for cards that standardizes typographic hierarchy, including title, subtitle, location, review rating, and pricing details.

sets.name: IconBtn
sets.description: Compact action button for icon-only interactions, such as favoriting, saving, or sharing, designed for image overlays or tight inline layouts.
